# Phillips

## Overview

- **Age:** Adult  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P27](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0027)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P40](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0040)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolmaster at Avonlea school  <sub>[v1 c15 P8](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0008), [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Phillips is a schoolmaster who curls his mustache.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)_

## Personality

Mr. Phillips exhibits severe sarcasm and a vindictive spirit when disciplining students. He suffers from spasmodic fits of reform regarding school discipline and order. He shows open favoritism toward older students, particularly Prissy Andrews, while neglecting younger pupils. His teaching lacks imagination and proper classroom management.

_Sources: [v1 c11 P33](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0033), [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P57](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0057), [v1 c15 P65](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0065), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)_

## Traits

- Sarcastic  <sub>[v1 c15 P61](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0061), [v1 c15 P65](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0065), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002)</sub>
- Partial and favoring older pupils  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>
- Inconsistent disciplinarian  <sub>[v1 c15 P57](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0057), [v1 c15 P60](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0060)</sub>
- Lacking imagination  <sub>[v1 c11 P33](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0033)</sub>

## Abilities

- Teaching Latin, algebra, geometry, French, and other school subjects  <sub>[v1 c15 P27](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0027), [v1 c15 P31](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0031), [v1 c17 P37](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0037)</sub>
- Elocution and reciting dramatic speeches  <sub>[v1 c19 P39](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0039)</sub>

## Goals

- Prepare older students for the entrance examination into Queen's Academy  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>
- Court Prissy Andrews  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c18 P10](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0010)</sub>

## History

Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster of Avonlea school, where he frequently spent class time sitting with sixteen-year-old student Prissy Andrews to explain her lessons and write on her slate. During his tenure, he humiliated Anne Shirley on her first day by holding up her slate due to spelling errors, and later punished her for breaking a slate over Gilbert Blythe by forcing her to stand at the blackboard. On another occasion, after a sudden decision to punish latecomers, he singled out Anne and made her sit next to Gilbert Blythe, prompting Anne to quit school for several weeks. At the Debating Club concert in aid of the library, he recited Mark Antony's oration over the body of Caesar. At the end of June, he gave an affecting farewell speech with tears in his eyes as his time as schoolmaster ended.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P46](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0046), [v1 c15 P57](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0057), [v1 c15 P61](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0061), [v1 c19 P33](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0033), [v1 c19 P39](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0039), [v1 c21 P0](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0000), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002)_

## Background by volume

- Secured his teaching position at Avonlea because his uncle was a school trustee  <sub>[v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091)</sub>

## Quotes

> Anne Shirley, what does this mean?  <sub>[v1 c15 P41](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0041)</sub>

> I am sorry to see a pupil of mine displaying such a temper and such a vindictive spirit, Anne, go and stand on the platform in front of the blackboard for the rest of the afternoon.  <sub>[v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044)</sub>

> Anne Shirley, since you seem to be so fond of the boys’ company we shall indulge your taste for it this afternoon, Take those flowers out of your hair and sit with Gilbert Blythe.  <sub>[v1 c15 P61](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0061)</sub>

> The time has come for us to part.  <sub>[v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002)</sub>

### Prissy Andrews

### Anne Shirley

- Mentor of — Taught him in the fourth book at Avonlea school.  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)</sub>
